q: Compare the characters of Siddhartha and Devadatta in terms of their values, actions, and consequences. How do their differences impact the story?

Devadatta values power, pride, and hunting. His cruel action of shooting an innocent swan and demanding its possession shows his greed and lack of sympathy. Consequently, he faces humiliation and failure in court.

Their sharp contrast creates the main conflict of the story and helps establish the moral principle that life belongs to the protector, not the destroyer.

q: Write the summary of the poem "Somebody's Mother" in your own words.
ans:
The poem 'Somebody's Mother' by Mary Dow Brine highlights the values of empathy, compassion, and selfless service. On a cold, snowy winter day, an old woman dressed in ragged clothes stands at a busy crossing, afraid to cross the slippery road due to heavy carriage traffic. Nobody in the crowd pays attention to her plight.

Soon, a group of cheerful schoolboys passes by. One kind-hearted boy notices her helplessness, stops playing, and offers to help. He gently holds her trembling arm and assists her safely to the other side. Later, he tells his friends that she is 'somebody's mother' and hopes that someday someone will lend a helping hand to his own mother if she is old and poor. That night, the old woman prays to God to be kind to the noble boy who helped her.

I felt it was my moral duty as a young, capable person to assist someone who was weak and vulnerable. After all, she is somebody's mother, aged and loved by her family. I thought of my own mother and hoped that if she ever found herself old, lonely, and in need on a distant street, some kind stranger would extend a gentle hand to guide her. True happiness lies in helping others selflessly.
